is: The identity nouns: user, account, membership, invitation, role, actor identity, handle, custody keys, PLC operations, character, profile and public records.
conventions: Each file owns its id type, value objects, and pure invariant logic.
The serde-deriving id newtypes are `Did`, `UserId` and `AccountId` — the CLI identity file needs them.

Ids derive `FromStr` forwarding to the inner type's error (`uuid::Error` for Uuid-backed ids, `DidParseError` for Did-backed ids); `From`/`Into`/`AsRef`/`Display` likewise forward, with no `Deref` and no `new` wrapper. Every error type is a `thiserror` derive.

Enum vocabularies derive strum (Display, EnumString, IntoStaticStr, VariantArray; serialize_all = snake_case), keep their typed Unknown* parse errors through parse_err_ty/parse_err_fn, and pin their literal token list in the sibling tests.rs; no hand-written ALL consts or as_str tables.

notes: Persisted enums (`ActorKind`, `ActorState`, `InvitationState`, `Role`) own their storage tokens: renaming one is a migration, and an unknown token is always an error, never a silent default.
See also: ZMVP-48 (handle.rs, a plain `//` body comment left in place — the punycode reject test section).

The reserved-label gate follows the configured `HandleDomain` (ruling R-77, 2026-10-12): `Handle::ensure_unreserved` refuses the namespace's bare apex (`NamespaceApex`) and any member whose leftmost label is in `RESERVED_LABELS` (`ReservedLabel`); the application's `ensure_handle_claimable` calls it first, so every claim path passes it, `change_handle` calls it before its namespace check, and the `/.well-known/atproto-did` resolver refuses a withheld handle before any lookup. `HandleDomain` must itself parse as a `Handle` (a bare hostname: no `*`, port, scheme or path, no IP literal). Under staging's `zurfur.foo`, `admin.zurfur.foo` is refused and `admin.zurfur.app` is an ordinary BYO handle.
